text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2% today as oil prices weakened, with US crude dropping to $89.62 per barrel despite ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The stock has retreated steadily over the past week, losing roughly 4% from its peak of $142.28 on November 13th, even as Iran escalates military threats against U.S. forces and infrastructure in the Gulf region and the IEA warns that confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor has been "crushed." This suggests the market is currently focused on near-term demand concerns and economic softness—like record UK diesel prices pushing inflation higher—rather than pricing in a supply shock from regional conflict.

The disconnect between rising geopolitical risk and falling oil prices reflects investor skepticism about whether these tensions will actually disrupt flows through one of the world's most critical chokepoints, or whether markets simply expect demand to soften enough to offset any supply fears.
